content_voiceover: The C-N-S I-P-I predicts risk of central nervous system relapse in diffuse large B cell lymphoma, which is a distinct and clinically important question from general prognosis. It uses the same five classic I-P-I factors, age over sixty, advanced Ann Arbor stage, E-C-O-G performance status two or higher, elevated L-D-H, and more than one extranodal site, each worth one point, and adds a sixth factor: kidney or adrenal gland involvement, also one point. Total score defines three risk groups: low, zero to one point; intermediate, two to three points; and high, four to six points. The Kaplan-Meier data show the two year probability of C-N-S relapse rises from roughly two to three percent in the low risk group, to around four to five percent in intermediate risk, up to approximately twelve percent in the high risk group. Critically, once C-N-S relapse occurs, overall survival is dismal, dropping sharply within the first several months, which is why identifying high risk patients matters, since it guides decisions about C-N-S directed prophylaxis such as intrathecal or high dose methotrexate.
keypoints: CNS-IPI = 5 classic IPI factors plus kidney or adrenal involvement (1 point each)
CNS relapse probability rises from ~2-3% (low) to ~12% (high risk)
OS after CNS relapse occurs is very poor, dropping sharply within months
High CNS-IPI score guides decisions on CNS-directed prophylaxis
